decisions.question: Bring the September seam chain to dev by replaying it, by re-deriving it, or by building on #8854's boundary in slices?

options.label: Build on #8854 in slices
options.gains: one boundary that the co-maintainer wrote and the follow-up list already names; slices fit the merge-dev-in, child-PR workflow; dev's #8845 and #8841 rules stay where they are
options.risks: the seam's filter AST, PostgreSQL backend and red controls are rebuilt rather than reused; #8854's open contract questions gate the later slices

options.label: Replay the old chain
options.gains: reuses September's commits and their tests
options.risks: 30 conflicting paths in one merge; 14 internal merges; two parts already on dev in another form; a second boundary beside #8854

options.label: Re-derive without #8854
options.gains: a clean design from the specs
options.risks: duplicates #8854's slot and its gate; the most new review

decisions.question: Does #8854 land in 16.0.0, and is it aligned with the write-path plans first? The differences are its event, the socket's [] refusal, the Nightscout-Data-Warnings header and the write-step name.

options.label: B: aligned first, in 16.0.0 (the maintainer's lean)
options.gains: 16.0.0 ships the boundary with nothing client-visible undecided
options.risks: 16.0.0 waits for the alignment and a re-run of the 67-shape client replay

options.label: D: split; the internal parts in 16.0.0, the header and socket validation decided first
options.gains: the boundary, gates and guards ship without waiting on the header and socket decisions
options.risks: two PRs; the client replay re-run covers the internal parts

options.label: C: as is in 16.0.0
options.risks: the header and the socket [] refusal ship as public behaviour in a major

decisions.question: One event per call carrying the stored records, or one per driver operation with counts only; and does a socket refusal acknowledge [] for the whole batch?

options.label: Per call, with _id and identifier (internal)
options.gains: one fact per write for caches, the change feed (T4) and a future tenant broadcast
options.risks: changes #8854's contract; payload must stay off public channels

options.label: Per driver operation, counts only (as drafted)
options.risks: the change feed cannot name records from it

decisions.question: On a merge, does an explicit null remove the field (identity §3, sync-transport T2, write contract §6.1) or store null (#8845 on dev)?

options.label: Null removes the field
options.gains: matches three written specs and the 2026-10-12 decision

decisions.question: Send the reply to the Loop maintainers, then settle format, client _id, absent identifier, re-send after delete, scope and immutability (six ID-*-DECISION items).

options.label: Send after ID-SIMPLE-MATCH is a PR
options.gains: the reply can point at a working change

options.label: Send now
options.risks: asks about behaviour not yet built

decisions.question: When a v1 entry's identifier is not yet stored, does it still match a stored reading at the same time and type (as dev does today, pinned by TEST-ENTRY-UUID-003), or only ever match on identifier, as v1 treatments do?

options.label: Keep the time-key fallback (as built)
options.gains: no change for readings whose app ids change; TEST-ENTRY-UUID-003 stays green
options.risks: a new identifier at a stored time takes over that reading, as today

options.label: Identifier only, like treatments
options.gains: one rule for entries and treatments
options.risks: two readings stored at one time when an app's ids change; an existing test changes

decisions.question: The setting is built as CONTROLLER_REGISTRATION (on/off, default off). Keep it, or use a staged mode (off, catalogue, submit) like WRITE_VALIDATION? Also: the vendored catalogue's home (lib/registration/catalogue/), the one-hour cache, and the older proposal schemas in docs/proposals/ on dev (left in place for now).

options.label: Proposal in the slice's PR body
options.gains: decided with the code in view

decisions.question: Approve the DECISION sections of the tenant-owner configuration surface (what a tenant may set, what the hoster pins).

options.label: Walk through the sections
options.gains: unblocks the config table and every hosted entrypoint
options.risks: the census was taken on the old chain and is re-measured on dev first

options.label: Client identifier kept, as dev does
options.gains: one rule across hubs for controllers

options.label: Hub-specific, declared in the capability document
